info.name: SIEMantics - Test Scenarios
info.description:
Manual/automated test scenarios for the SIEMantics SOAR API. Mirrors scripts/test_requests.sh: covers the mock-engine severity threshold, all 9 suspicious-pattern regexes, IoC extraction, edge cases, labeling and metrics, plus the IRIS case content, users, case assignment and auth.

Run order matters: folders 1-3 create the alert records that folder 4 refers to. Use Collection Runner to execute the whole collection top to bottom, or run folder by folder.

Set the `base_url` and `webhook_token` collection variables (Variables tab) to match your deployment. If WAZUH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN isn't set server-side, `webhook_token` can be left empty.

Alert IDs: every stored alert gets a unique `ID-<number>`. A collection-level test checks this format on every alert response and saves it as `ref_<wazuh alert id>` (non-alphanumerics -> `_`, e.g. `ref_test_sqli_union`), so later requests can refer to the exact record.

Folders 4-5 and 7-9 need a logged-in dashboard user (admin): set `ui_username` / `ui_password` - the Login request at the start of folders 4, 7, 8 and 9 stores the session cookie in Postman's cookie jar.

Folder 6 holds realistic alerts in the full Wazuh format from several sources. Folder 7 creates IRIS cases that exercise every part of the case content (see its description for what to check in IRIS). Folder 8 tests the correlation of similar alerts from the same source IP into one case. Folder 9 covers users, case assignment and the analyst/admin permission rules; it ends by logging out.

True-positive requests accept both 202 (escalated) and 502 (IRIS unreachable), so the collection also runs without an IRIS instance.

item.name: 6. Realistic multi-source Wazuh alerts
item.description:
Realistic alerts in the full Wazuh alert format (rule.groups/mitre, agent, manager, decoder, location, data.*) as forwarded by the Wazuh integration. Besides Wazuh's own rules they cover sources that reach Wazuh through its decoders/integrations: web access logs, FIM (syscheck), vulnerability detector, ClamAV, Suricata EVE, Windows Security + Sysmon (eventchannel), FortiGate syslog, AWS CloudTrail and Office 365.

Each request name ends in '-> TP' or '-> FP' = the expected ground truth, for labelling/evaluation. Some are deliberately hard for the rule-based mock engine (e.g. Suricata alerts are always level 3 in Wazuh, an authorized internal scan is level 10), so they show where the LLM adds value. The tests only assert the API contract; the verdict vs. expectation is printed to the Postman console.

Alert IDs, IPs, hashes and rule IDs are sample data (rule IDs follow the Wazuh ruleset where one exists, custom rules use the 100000+ range).

item.name: 7. IRIS case content (L2 / Lead Analyst)
item.description:
Creates IRIS cases that exercise every part of the case content built for L2 analysts and Lead Analysts. The API only returns the case ID/URL (printed to the Postman console), the content itself must be checked in IRIS - each request's description says what to look for.

Check in IRIS (manually, the API does not return the case content):
- name: `[SIEMantics ID-<n>] [P1/CRITICAL] <rule> @ <host>`
- description: verdict + key facts table (rule, MITRE links, host/agent, source IP:port, target user, log source, IoCs) + first L2 steps
- notes group `SIEMantics ID-<n>` with 5 notes: triage summary, alert details (compliance, MITRE, data.* fields), threat intelligence, investigation checklist (pivot queries, Lead Analyst criteria), raw evidence (full JSON)
- IOCs with type (ip-any / domain / url / sha256 when extracted by the LLM), description and `siemantics,ID-<n>,T...` tags
- asset: the agent host (Linux - Server / Windows - Computer), status 'To be done'
- case severity and tags (`ID-<n>`, `P1`, `severity:critical`, MITRE IDs, tactics)
- timeline: one event at the Wazuh event time (with its timezone), category = first MITRE tactic (Unspecified without MITRE), linked to the asset and the IOCs, raw log in the raw field, shown in summary and graph

item.name: 8. Correlation (same source IP + similar alert)
item.description:
Alerts from the same source IP (`data.srcip`, the agent IP does not count) are added to the existing open IRIS case if they are similar: same Wazuh rule ID, or a shared MITRE technique (sub-techniques count as their base technique, e.g. T1110.001 ~ T1110.003), within CORRELATION_WINDOW_HOURS (default 24). A closed case is never extended - a new case is opened instead.

Each run uses a fresh random source IP (198.18.x.y), so earlier runs do not interfere. The assertions only run when the first alert was escalated (with an LLM the verdicts may differ; IRIS down -> 502).
